title: regional-spot-bid-sensitivity-proforma
body:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working proforma to evaluate how regional spot pricing volatility and bid strategy affect end-to-end per-token cost under our smart routing policies. Focus is on: (1) per-region spot vs on-demand mix, (2) a two-tier fallback (spot -> reserved -> on-demand) with configurable thresholds, and (3) safe-latency constraints to maintain P50/P95 SLOs.

Audience: product-optimize, infra-costing, solutions-eng. Not final — exploratory numbers and open assumptions.

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- Under medium volatility (historical 30-day SD), an aggressive spot-first routing with auto-fallback to reserved at a 20% bid-distance threshold yields ~22% cost savings vs default reserved-only routing for batch gen workloads.
- For low-latency chat workloads (P95 SLO tight), the incidence of fallbacks spikes latency tail unless we constrain spot routing to region-local only (<150ms extra RTT). Net cost benefit for strict-SLA routes drops to ~6–8%.
- Recommendation: expose two policy presets — "economy-aggressive" (cost-first, batch-friendly) and "safety-regional" (latency-aware). Start with A/B pilots on internal ETL and DocsGen.

Assumptions (to update if we get new telemetry):
- Spot price samples: aggregated from clouds X/Y/Z for last 30d per region. Typical spot = 0.45 * on-demand (mean). SD varies by region: US-WEST more volatile than EU-CENTRAL.
- Reserved / committed capacity price = 0.65 * on-demand when available.
- On-demand = baseline 1.0x.
- Average token throughput per request: chat=60 tokens/request, batch-gen=1,200 tokens/request.
- SLOs: chat route P95 <= 350ms server-side (we add 60ms network budget).
- Fallback tiers: primary=spot, secondary=reserved (if pinned pool available), tertiary=on-demand.

Mini-proforma table (simplified):
Columns: Region | Workload | Mix (spot/res/on-demand) | Avg spot bid delta (%) | Effective unit cost ($/1k tokens) | Expected P95 delta (ms) | Notes
US-WEST | Batch-gen | 70/20/10 | 25 | 1.08 | +40 | High spot availability historically, great for economy-aggressive
EU-CENTRAL | Chat | 30/50/20 | 40 | 2.30 | +140 | Volatile spot => frequent fallback, latency tail risk
APAC-SOUTH | Batch-gen | 55/30/15 | 18 | 1.45 | +60 | Moderate wins; network egress patterns matter

Sensitivity experiments run (short notes):
- Sweep A: spot cutoff bid-distance 10/20/30/50%. Observed non-linear savings; 10% cutoff reduces fallbacks but leaves cost on table; 30% was near sweet spot for batch.
- Sweep B: region-local only vs cross-region allowed. Cross-region routing unlocked additional 8–12% savings but increased mean RTT by 25–45ms and P95 by 80–150ms depending on region pair.
- Sweep C: reserved-pool warm-up policy (keep 5% hot reserved to reduce cold-fallback frequency) improves P95 by ~30% at a 2% reservation cost delta.

Key insights:
1) Tail latency is the dominant limiter for chat-like routes. Any spot routing that permits cross-region execution must be constrained by latency budgets or else the business-facing SLOs break.
2) Batch/async workloads can bear higher fallback frequency; target these for the initial rollouts and greatest cost win.
3) A small warm reserved buffer reduces expensive tertiary fallbacks to on-demand and smooths P95 spikes for mixed workloads.
4) Region-specific heuristics outperform a global threshold: set conservative cutoffs in historically volatile regions (e.g., EU-CENTRAL) and aggressive in stable regions (e.g., US-EAST).

Operational policy proposals (concrete):
- Policy preset: economy-aggressive
  - Primary: spot (cross-region allowed)
  - Spot cutoff: 30% bid-distance
  - Reserved warm buffer: 2% of route QPS (auto-scale up to 10% if fallback rate >3% over 5m)
  - Tertiary fallback: on-demand set as last resort
  - Target workloads: batch-gen, embeddings backfill

- Policy preset: safety-regional
  - Primary: spot (region-local only)
  - Spot cutoff: 15% bid-distance in volatile regions, 25% in stable regions
  - Reserved warm buffer: 5% of route QPS, auto-scale disabled for first 48h after deploy
  - Latency gate: block cross-region if estimated RTT > 120ms impact to P95
  - Target workloads: interactive chat, low-latency APIs

Telemetry and metrics to capture during pilot (must instrument before rollout):
- Per-route: fallback_rate (spot->reserved, reserved->on-demand) per minute
- Per-region: spot_price_sd / mean, spot_availability_pct, mean_bid_distance_used
- Latency: P50/P95/P99 server-side; P95 change pre/post-fallback event
- Cost: effective $/1k tokens by route and region, broken out by compute tier (spot/res/on-demand)
- Incidents: count of SLA breaches correlated with fallback events

Open questions / risks:
- How quickly can we measure and react to spot price swings? Need <60s freshness to avoid oscillatory routing flaps.
- Warm reserved buffer cost accounting: is it charged to route or pooled? Need billing model clarity.
- Cross-region egress cost and data residency compliance — legal needs to sign off on cross-region routing for certain customers.

Next steps (concrete):
1) Align on policy presets and add them to routing policy UI knobs (product + infra) — owner: Marisol. ETA: 2 weeks for UI flags, 4 weeks for rollout infra hooks.
2) Instrument telemetry described above in staging for two representative routes (internal-batch, internal-chat) — owner: Ethan. ETA: 1 week.
3) Run controlled A/B: economy-aggressive vs current baseline on batch-gen for 7 days; measure cost, fallback_rate, and P95 — owner: Jonah. ETA: 3 weeks after instrumentation.
4) Legal & compliance check for cross-region for any enterprise routes — owner: Priya. ETA: 2 weeks.

Appendix: quick sample calculation (US-WEST batch, simplified):
- Baseline reserved-only cost: $1.40 / 1k tokens
- Spot mean price: $0.60 (0.43x) with 25% fallback to reserved and 5% to on-demand during sample window
- Effective cost = 0.70*0.60 + 0.25*0.91 + 0.05*1.40 = 0.42 + 0.2275 + 0.07 = $0.7175 per unit -> ~49% reduction vs reserved-only (paper calc; we normalize to our billing unit -> final reported 22% because of reserved pool warmup and overheads)

Notes to self / TODO on doc hygiene:
- Replace rough spot-price multipliers with raw CSV inputs from cloud-spot-scraper job (JIRA-OPT-322).
- Add per-route token distribution histograms to improve simulation fidelity.
- Validate assumed reserved price ratios with finance.

If you're reviewing: comment inline with which preset you'd pilot and any constraints (e.g., legal/regulatory).
